title: Six basic routes
summary: Slant, out, curl, post, go, and drag: the shapes every receiver runs.

steps.text: A route is the path a receiver runs. Each one has a shape and a name. Run this demo play and watch each receiver. X runs a go: straight down the field as fast as possible. It is the deep shot.
H runs an out: a few yards upfield, then a sharp cut toward the sideline. Good for a quick, safe throw near the sideline.
Y runs a curl: run upfield about 10 yards, then stop and turn back toward the quarterback. The defender keeps running past you.
Z runs a post: deep, then angle toward the middle of the field, toward the goal posts. The running back runs a drag: a shallow route across the middle, right behind the linemen.

The sixth route is the slant. Three steps upfield, then a sharp cut inside at an angle. It is quick and hard to stop. Watch X run it on Slant-Flat. Go, out, curl, post, drag, slant: six shapes to spot on any diagram.

quiz.prompt: Which route goes straight down the field as fast as possible?
quiz.explanation: The go route is the deep straight line.

quiz.prompt: A receiver runs 10 yards, stops, and turns back to the quarterback. Which route?
quiz.explanation: Stop and turn back is a curl.

quiz.prompt: Tap the receiver running the post route, deep and then toward the middle.
quiz.explanation: Z runs the post: deep, then angled toward the goal posts.

quiz.prompt: Which route cuts sharply toward the sideline?
quiz.explanation: The out route breaks toward the sideline. The slant breaks inside.

quiz.prompt: Which route is a shallow path across the middle of the field?
quiz.explanation: The drag runs across the field just past the line of scrimmage.
